questions.question: int f(int n) { if (n==0) return 0; return n + f(n-1); } What does f(4) return?
void p(int n) { if(n==0) return; printf("%d ", n); p(n-1); printf("%d ", n); }  What does p(3) print?
questions.solutionApproach: Before-recursive-call print is forward, after-call print is reverse. Before prints: 3 2 1 (forward). After prints (as stack unwinds): 1 2 3 (reverse). Combined trace: 3(before,n=3) 2(before,n=2) 1(before,n=1) [base case n=0, returns] 1(after,n=1) 2(after,n=2) 3(after,n=3).

questions.question: int f(int n) { if(n<=1) return 1; return f(n-1)+f(n-1); } How many total calls to f() occur when f(4) is invoked (including the initial call)?
int g(int n) { static int total=0; total += n; if(n<=1) return total; return g(n-1); }  What does g(4) return?
questions.solutionApproach: total starts 0. g(4): total=0+4=4, calls g(3). g(3): total=4+3=7, calls g(2). g(2): total=7+2=9, calls g(1). g(1): total=9+1=10, n<=1 so returns total=10. This 10 propagates back up unchanged (each level just returns what g(n-1) returned).
